ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the graph, in the same Cartesian coordinate system, the graph of the linear function $y=-2x+4$ intersects with the graph of the direct proportion function $y=kx\ (k>0)$ at point A, and the y-coordinate of point A is 2. Then, what is the solution set for the inequality $kx>-2x+4$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since the graph of the linear function $y=-2x+4$ intersects with the graph of the directly proportional function $y=kx\ (k>0)$ at point $A$, and the ordinate of point $A$ is 2,\\
we substitute ${y}_{A}=2$ into $y=-2x+4$ to get: ${x}_{A}=1$,\\
Since $kx>-2x+4$,\\
it follows that $x>1$,\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{x>1}$.
